notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended November 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to county board and county office candidates, reported to the State Board of Elections since 2023 (none were found). Illinois allows business contributions. Individuals, candidates' own money, party and candidate committees, loans and other receipts are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2022, as the township reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Jersey County.
Illinois townships maintain township roads, assess property and provide general assistance; most also cover the cities and villages inside them.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money is not scored: no candidates for mayor or village president, council or board, clerk and other local offices of Rosedale Township reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside Rosedale Township's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-18.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Illinois yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
